correctness.rationale: For each n>=2, the 2^(n-1) specific nondyadic rational angular points have all length-(n-1) binary itineraries and identical starting fibers. The coordinate change u=x+y,q=y/u gives u_next=alpha*u and q_next=2q mod 1. Each first symbolic difference occurs at t<=n-2; equal prefixes force equal fiber z_t and the affine branch gap phi2(z_t)-phi1(z_t) is bounded below by delta=min(1-lambda1,1-lambda2)>0 on [0,1]. Their t+1 values differ at fixed epsilon<delta. Every common n-itinerary branch composition contracts in maximum norm by kappa<=max(2alpha,lambda1,lambda2)<1, so each of 2^n itineraries contributes at most (floor(1/epsilon)+1)^3 separated points, proving exact entropy log 2. All quantifiers, strict inequalities and the noncompact domain are specified. The standalone exact-Fraction checker verifies samples in four regimes and word lengths 1..8, but the proof for all n and all parameters is analytic.

originality.rationale: The motivating original exact model proves only h_top >= (log2)/k0, where k0>1 throughout the overlapping regime lambda1+lambda2>=1; its authors state that factor symbolic coding on the noncompact admissible set is insufficient to obtain full-shift entropy and note that the base g itself has zero entropy. The new synchronized-fiber construction proves a stronger sharp full-parameter fixed-scale bound, and its conclusion is not implied by their quantitative theorem. Kruglikov--Rypdal provide general multiplicity/skew-product bounds and an equality for genuinely compact symbolic base shifts, not a lower bound for the present noncompact contracting triangular base. value.rationale: This determines a previously non-exact invariant in the exact natural family of a published positive-entropy piecewise contraction, closes an explicit parameter-dependent factor loss in Proposition 5.3, and proves entropy stays maximal log2 even when its attractor changes from Cantor set to an interval. The synchronous common-fiber argument gives a reusable explanation of why overlapping image intervals need not reduce finite-time orbit separation; no unmotivated parameter slice or routine numerical recomputation is involved.
